$comment: Machine-readable source metadata for TASK-002 (docs/sources/pesel.md, D-001 in docs/DECISIONS_NEEDED.md). Fields kept explicitly separate per project-owner instruction: data_date, created, modified, verified and retrieved_at are never inferred from one another. Every field below is now populated from verified evidence; no value is inferred from a sibling field.

dataset.official_dataset_url_note: The previous value in this file was truncated mid-slug ('...1681,nazwis'), a transcription artefact. Corrected 2026-09-19 to the full landing-page form built from the confirmed dataset_slug. The API self-link below is the verified value read directly from the portal's own dataset response.
dataset.licence_provenance: Dataset-level license_name = 'CC0 1.0', read from the portal's own dataset metadata response. Resource-level metadata carries no licence, rights or terms field at all (checked across the full attribute set of all four 2026 resources), so resource inheritance of this licence is an assumption this project has NOT verified — see D-004 in docs/DECISIONS_NEEDED.md.

resources.format_supplied: CSV (portal-generated conversion served from the official csv_download_url endpoint)
resources.provenance: Verified twice, independently, from byte-identical copies: (1) file bytes supplied directly by the project owner during TASK-002; (2) an automated acquisition run by the project owner (NAME_ATLAS_ALL_DOWNLOADED_DATA archive, generated 2026-09-18T17:44:29Z) which downloaded the same resource from the official endpoint and recorded a matching SHA-256. This session verified the archive against its own SHA256SUMS.txt (46/46 OK) and confirmed both checksums match this manifest exactly. This session did not download from dane.gov.pl itself — it remained network-egress-blocked throughout.
resources.dates_note: data_date (2026-01-20) is the PESEL reference date; created/modified/verified (2026-01-28) are portal metadata timestamps and are a different, later date; retrieved_at is when the project owner fetched the bytes. Four distinct concepts — never infer one from another.
resources.source_url_fields_note: official_source_url is the portal's csv_download_url attribute — the stable endpoint to fetch from. official_source_media_file_url is the portal's csv_file_url attribute — the direct media-file URL for the same CSV, carrying a date-stamped path. Both are values read verbatim from the resource's own api.dane.gov.pl metadata response; neither was observed as an HTTP redirect by this session, which never reached the host. official_resource_metadata_url is the 1.4 API resource endpoint those attributes came from.

file_structure.quoting: none observed — no field in either file contains a comma or a literal quote character
file_structure.newline: CRLF (\r\n) throughout both files, no stray LF-only or CR-only lines; file ends with a trailing CRLF after the last data row
file_structure.bom: absent (confirmed from the first bytes: 4e 61 7a ... = literal "Naz...", not EF BB BF)
file_structure.sort_order: descending by Liczba, confirmed for the full file in both male and female resources

value_types.Nazwisko aktualne: non-empty string; observed alphabet spans plain A-Z, the full set of Polish diacritics (Ł Ś Ż Ź Ć Ń Ó Ą Ę), and a much wider set of Latin-extended, Vietnamese, Cyrillic and other script characters reflecting naturalised citizens; space, apostrophe, hyphen, period, parentheses and forward slash also occur in real values
value_types.Liczba: positive integer; observed range 2 to 99738 across both files; zero, negative and non-numeric values do not occur

file_structure.suppression_confirmed_from_bytes: No row with Liczba = 1 or Liczba = 0 exists in either file — directly confirms the dataset-level suppression rule (surnames occurring exactly once are excluded) from the actual bytes, not merely from portal metadata.
unicode_notes: All observed surname values are already NFC-normalised.

A small number of rows (7 in the male file, 5 in the female file) contain a base Latin letter followed by a standalone Unicode combining mark (e.g. "DOG̈AN", "GLA̋SSNER") for which no precomposed character exists — this is a property of the source data, not a parsing artefact, and must be preserved exactly, not repaired or re-mapped.

One row in the female file ("SCHIED ,2") has a trailing space in the surname field — a real data-quality artefact in the official source, preserved as-is in the fixture; do not silently trim surname values.

A small number of rows contain a forward slash within the surname (e.g. "A/GADIR", "W/SILASSIE", "W/RUFAEL") — real values, not delimiter confusion (confirmed: exactly 2 comma-separated fields on every such row).
